**p13:e108** - Figure explaining the real reason for 50ms reduction: CUDA context initialization warmup effect. When pre_upload_weights_to_gpu calls cudaMalloc and cudaMemcpy before t_start, the CUDA driver wakes up for the first time, causing:
1. GPU context initialization (CUDA driver load)
2. GPU clock boosting (low power → max performance frequency)
3. JIT compilation (first kernel code compilation)

These initialization costs are pushed outside the timer interval. In mempool version, ensure_pool() → first cudaMalloc is inside t_start, so all initialization costs are included in measurement.

mempool version: [initialization 50ms] + [actual computation] = measured
preload version: [initialization 50ms] + [actual computation] = initialization is outside timer!

So d_W wasn't used to speed up, but pre_upload_weights_to_gpu unintentionally served as GPU warmup, pushing initialization costs outside the timer. This is why first_try explicitly had warmup_cublas().
